title: Auto Loans: Fees Settled by a Payoff
content:
Paying off an Auto Loans account settles the fees on it along with everything else. This note defines the fees taken in when the borrower closes the loan with money moved from their own PCB checking account.

## Definition

The fees share of a payoff is the loan's fee balance as the loan's own activity shows it: all fees ever booked on the loan, minus all fee settlements, minus all fee waivers, to the cent. The balance moves only through entries on the loan; a fee leaves it when it is settled out of a payment or when a waiver of it is recorded. It is taken as it stands at the moment the payoff figure is set, and the payoff settles it in full.

## Principle

A payoff is the final settlement of what the borrower properly owes. It never takes in a fee that PCB's bank-error test for returned payment fees, or its bank-error test for late charges, identifies as having been charged contrary to the Auto Loans rules. Every other fee in the balance is collected in full through the fees share.

## Illustrations (invented activity)

| Fees booked | Settlements | Waivers | Fees share of the payoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| 52.40 | 27.40 | 0.00 | 25.00 |
| 60.00 | 0.00 | 35.00 | 25.00 |
| 25.00 | 25.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
